issues.legal_issue: A reference application is not barred solely because it was filed more than six weeks after receipt of a notice of the award when the notice was not accompanied by a copy of the award.
material_facts: The applicant was absent when the award was made and received a notice of the award from the Collector.
The notice was not accompanied by a copy of the award; the applicant obtained a certified copy through an advocate and then applied for a reference.
The State produced no evidence that a copy of the award had been sent with the notice.
The Reference Court and the High Court treated the application as late without considering the absence of the copy.
issues.conclusion: The application was not barred on the basis relied on by the lower courts, which erred in rejecting the reference as time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12(2) and 18(1) and (2)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 require notice of the award to enable an interested person to exercise the right to seek a reference effectively; a copy of the award should accompany the notice. The limitation principles in Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Land Acquisition Officer, AIR 1961 SC 1500, State of Punjab v. Qaisar Jehan Begum, AIR 1963 SC 1604, and Bhagwan Das v. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2010) 3 SCC 545, recognize the importance of knowledge of the essential contents of the award.

rule.if: compensation_reference_application and notice_received and notice_lacked_award_copy and application_filed_after_notice_based_limit

predicates.compensation_reference_application: An interested person applied to have a land-acquisition compensation dispute referred for determination.
predicates.notice_received: The interested person received notice that the award had been made.
predicates.notice_lacked_award_copy: The notice delivered to the interested person did not include a copy of the award.
predicates.application_filed_after_notice_based_lim: The interested person filed the reference application after the period ordinarily measured from receipt of the notice.

issues.definition: When an interested person seeks a compensation reference, receives notice without the award copy, and applies after the ordinary notice-based period, the application is not barred on that timing basis.

issues.legal_issue: Enhanced compensation and statutory benefits may be extended to similarly situated landowners who did not pursue appeals when the Court considers that course appropriate in the case.
material_facts: Other landowners whose land was acquired in the same scheme had sought enhanced compensation in related proceedings.
Some did not file appeals before the High Court, and others did not approach the Supreme Court.
The Court considered it a fit case to extend the relief granted to the appellant to those landowners as well.
issues.conclusion: The Court exercised its power under Article 142 of the Constitution and directed that the other landowners also receive enhanced compensation and statutory benefits.
issues.legal_principle: Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Court to make orders necessary to do complete justice. The Court considered its approach consistent with B. N. Nagarajan v. State of Mysore, (1966) 3 SCR 682; Bhupinderpal Singh v. State of Punjab, (2000) 5 SCC 262; Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa, (1993) 2 SCC 746; and B. Prabhakar Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, 1985 (Supp) SCC 432.

rule.if: related_land_acquisition_claims and claimants_similarly_situated and claimants_did_not_pursue_appeals and court_finds_collective_relief_appropriate

predicates.related_land_acquisition_claims: The claims arose from land acquired together in the same scheme and were addressed in related proceedings.
predicates.claimants_similarly_situated: The claimants who did not appeal were similarly situated to claimants who obtained relief.
predicates.claimants_did_not_pursue_appeals: Some of the similarly situated claimants did not pursue appeals to the higher courts.
predicates.court_finds_collective_relief_appropriat: The Court considered extending the relief to the nonappealing claimants appropriate in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When related claimants are similarly situated, some have not pursued appeals, and the Court considers collective relief appropriate, the relief is extended to those nonappealing claimants.
